themes.title: General-purpose humanoids
themes.description: Unitree priced the first pure-play humanoid IPO (Aug 6, $9B valuation). Figure 03 has passed 1,000 units in production (~1/hour), AgiBot has shipped ~15,000 cumulative units, and Boston Dynamics' Atlas is now shipping to Hyundai RMAC and Google DeepMind. Tesla Optimus remains the outlier — zero verified production a year into the line conversion.

themes.title: Warehouse & logistics automation
themes.description: Still the most commercially proven sub-sector. Symbotic's Q3 FY26 revenue hit $721M (+22% YoY) with GAAP net income of $55M — the backlog is now converting to real, growing profit, not just promises; Q4 guide of $760-780M revenue implies the growth is continuing.

themes.title: Surgical robotics
themes.description: ISRG's Q2 beat did not stop the bleeding — shares are down ~34% YTD as multiples compress, and sell-side opinion has split (UBS upgraded to Buy at $500 while HSBC cut to Hold). J&J Ottava and Medtronic Hugo continue to press the competitive case.

themes.title: Defense autonomy & drones
themes.description: AeroVironment's fiscal Q4 revenue more than doubled to $641.6M (Autonomous Systems now 76% of sales) and Kratos beat Q2 estimates while raising FY26 organic growth guidance to 19-23% — backlogs are now visibly converting to revenue, not just growing on paper. Pentagon FY27 budget still requests ~$75B for unmanned/counter-drone systems.

themes.title: Field robotics
themes.description: Deere's autonomous articulated dump truck continues quarry operations under its 2nd-gen autonomy kit; Caterpillar's five-machine autonomous construction lineup remains in early rollout. Both remain diversified industrials where robotics is a small slice of the overall return.

themes.title: Japanese factory automation
themes.description: Sentiment reversed hard: Fanuc shares suffered their worst single-day fall in 40 years on Aug 3 after FY27 guidance (¥218B operating income) missed estimates despite Q1 net profit rising 35% — rising material and component costs are now the story, just weeks after the stock hit limit-up on the same guidance narrative.

themes.title: Supply chain & components
themes.description: Regal Rexnord and FANUC unveiled an integrated cobot transfer-unit solution (Aug 4); Cognex remains a reference vision supplier as factories go software-defined. MP Materials beat Q2 revenue estimates by 13% and expects to begin shipping magnets from its Independence facility in H2 2026 — the transition from miner to magnet maker is now underway.

themes.title: The robot "brain"
themes.description: NVIDIA's Jetson Thor platform now counts 2M+ developers and early adopters including Agility, Amazon Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Caterpillar, Figure, Hexagon, Medtronic and Meta; new T3000/T2000 modules are slated for Q1 2027. Foundation-model startups Skild AI (~$14-15B val.) and Physical Intelligence (~$11B, in talks) continue racing to be the software layer.

themes.title: China scaling & listing
themes.description: Unitree priced its Shanghai STAR Market IPO at 150.8 yuan/share (~$9.04B valuation, ~$904M raised) on Aug 6 — China's first listed humanoid maker, with DeepSeek among strategic investors; retail subscription opened Aug 10, trading expected Aug 17-21. LimX ($2.2B pre-IPO) and Agibot continue prepping Hong Kong listings amid 150+ competing Chinese humanoid startups.

bear_case.title: Bubble warnings from serious sources
bear_case.description: China's NDRC has warned of a humanoid "bubble"; Morgan Stanley flags a wide gap between hype and scalability. New data sharpens the picture: the median disclosed humanoid round (Aug 2025-Jun 2026) was $145M, with rounds above $50M now 84% of all disclosed capital — and outliers like South Korea's Tomorrow Robotics have jumped 15x in valuation without a single confirmed commercial deployment.

bear_case.title: Demos ≠ autonomy
bear_case.description: If a humanoid demo isn't explicitly labeled autonomous, assume teleoperation. Dexterity, inference speed, reliability, and cost still confine real use to structured factory/warehouse tasks.

bear_case.title: Crowding & shakeout risk
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chasing humanoids; a reshuffling of startups is widely expected. Robotics pioneer Rodney Brooks argues much of the investment will be wasted.

bear_case.title: Guidance can evaporate fast
bear_case.description: Fanuc suffered its worst single-day fall in 40 years on Aug 3 despite Q1 profit +35%, purely on FY guidance missing estimates. Serve Robotics cut FY26 revenue guidance 65% (to $9-10M from $26M) after its core Uber partnership saw utilization decline for the first time in 17 quarters. ISRG is down 34% YTD despite beating Q2 estimates. In parts of this sector, sentiment is doing more work than fundamentals — in both directions.

bear_case.title: Revenue is elsewhere
bear_case.description: Industrial, logistics, and surgical robots generate proven revenue today; humanoids largely don't yet. Component and warehouse names carry less thesis risk than humanoid pure-plays.

bear_case.title: China price war
bear_case.description: Unitree's $5,900 R1 signals aggressive price compression that could squeeze Western OEM margins before the market matures — and 150+ Chinese humanoid startups are now competing on price.

bear_case.title: "Dot-com stage" warnings
bear_case.description: KB Securities likened 2026's robotics/space enthusiasm to the final stage of the dot-com bubble; Ray Dalio separately compared the broader AI bubble to 1929 and 2000 valuation extremes. Sector EV/EBITDA multiples ranged from 0.9x (mature industrials) to 78.2x (speculative pure-plays) in Q4 2025 — a valuation split investors should not treat as one trade.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Symbotic
positions.note: Q3 FY26 revenue $721M (+22% YoY) and GAAP net income of $55M (vs. a loss a year ago) confirm the backlog is converting to real, growing profit, not just a promise.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Jetson Thor now has 2M+ developers and adopters from Agility to Boston Dynamics to Figure — the default robot brain. It's also your largest AI-sleeve name, so check total exposure before adding here.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.note: Q2 revenue +19% YoY, yet the stock is down 34% YTD and sell-side has split (UBS Buy $500 PT vs. HSBC's downgrade to Hold). The growth was never in question — the price is what makes it interesting.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: Machine vision sells into every OEM regardless of which humanoid wins. EPS +112.5% last quarter and it is not priced as an AI name.

positions.name: Rockwell Automation
positions.note: The cleanest listed US factory-automation exposure, at a valuation that does not require humanoids to work.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: Fiscal Q4 revenue more than doubled to $641.6M, beating estimates by ~25% on EPS — the backlog is converting faster than expected. Still overlaps with your Defense sleeve; own it in one place, not both.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Q2 revenue beat guidance and management raised FY26 organic growth guidance to 19-23% — execution is now showing up in the numbers, not just the multiple.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: Optimus still has zero verified production a year into the line conversion, and Musk himself called it the hardest product Tesla has ever tried to scale. The option value is intact; the timeline keeps slipping.

positions.name: Harmonic Drive
positions.note: Pure leverage to humanoid build rates via actuators and reducers. Small, illiquid and awkward to access from the UK.

positions.name: Teradyne
positions.note: Universal Robots/MiR just posted a first-ever $100M quarter, +33% YoY — a real inflection. Still primarily a semiconductor-test stock wearing a robotics label; size accordingly.

positions.name: Deere & Co
positions.note: The autonomy kit is real and revenue-generating, but robotics is a rounding error next to the ag cycle you would actually be buying.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.note: Five-machine autonomous lineup rolling out — same problem as Deere: construction demand dominates the return.

positions.name: Fanuc
positions.note: Worst single-day fall in 40 years on Aug 3 after FY27 guidance missed — the July limit-up rally reversed just as fast. Wait for the volatility to settle before treating this as a re-rating.

positions.name: Keyence
positions.note: Exceptional margins and permanently expensive. Needs a genuine de-rating before the maths works.

positions.name: ABB Ltd
positions.note: Selling the robotics division to SoftBank for $5.375B — still awaiting regulatory clearance and not yet closed, which removes most of the reason it was on this list.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Q2 beat by 13% and magnet sales from Independence begin H2 2026 — real progress from miner to magnet maker. Sits in your Critical Minerals sleeve; don't double-count it here.

positions.name: Serve Robotics
positions.note: Q2 revenue grew 404% YoY but management slashed FY26 guidance 65% (to $9-10M from $26M) after Uber robot utilization fell for the first time in 17 straight quarters — the platform-dependency risk just became real.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: RPA is being disrupted by the same AI agents it claims to ride, and the robotics label is marketing rather than hardware.

positions.name: Ouster
positions.note: Shares keep rallying (+6% Aug 3) on sector sentiment, but lidar remains a commodity price war with no evidence of durable margin at any listed player.
